label: cor:ftc_eval
title: Evaluation of integrals via antiderivatives
statement:
Let $f$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and $F$ be a continuous antiderivative of $f$ on $(\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$. Then
    \[
      \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
    \]
proof: Let $G(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_is_antiderivative}, $G$ is an antiderivative of $f$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant}, $F(b) - G(b) = F(a) - G(a)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_func_at_base}, $G(a) = 0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:constant_diff_rearrangement}, $G(b) = F(b) - F(a)$.
